Andy Biggs

Republican candidate for Governor and Lieutenant Governor, Arizona · Challenger

U.S. Representative for Arizona's 5th Congressional District

Andy Biggs is a Republican who has represented Arizona's 5th Congressional District in the U.S. House since 2017. He won the Republican primary for governor in 2026. He is running in the November 3, 2026 general election with Sine Kerr as his lieutenant governor candidate.

Where Biggs stands

Taxes
Supports eliminating Arizona's state income tax and says he would take the first step toward that goal. Also supports working with local entities to reduce property taxes.
Affordability and housing
Says affordability is the top concern he hears from voters. Proposes codifying the repeal of what he calls Gov. Hobbs' housing moratorium on new single-family homes in fast-growing areas.
Water
Says water is the issue he is asked about most and argues the state cannot conserve its way out of shortages. He points to a bill he introduced in Congress for $19 billion in federal water infrastructure funding.
Data centers
Opposes additional tax breaks and subsidies for data centers. Says data centers should generate their own energy, avoid straining the power grid and water supply, and recycle water.
Energy and fuel prices
Proposes lowering fuel prices by reducing Arizona's reliance on California for fuel and increasing supply from other sources.
Health care and vaccines
Supports ending medical mandates and 'ensuring vaccine freedom.' Has released a health policy platform aligned with Make America Healthy Again (MAHA).
Education
Lists support for Arizona's Empowerment Scholarship Account (ESA) program among his priorities as governor.

Background

  • U.S. Representative, Arizona's 5th Congressional District, 2017–present

  • Republican nominee for Governor of Arizona, 2026
